title: Pinpoint capture handoff
description: The machine-readable form of an annotated capture. Written by Pinpoint to ~/Library/Application Support/Pinpoint/last/capture.json on every copy (next to capture.png and capture.md), to ~/Library/Application Support/Pinpoint/archive/<timestamp>/ as a timestamped copy, and to any path chosen through "Export JSON…" — where the two file paths below are absent because there are no siblings to point at. Coordinates are pixels from the top-left corner of the image described by `image`, then the same value as a percentage of it. `schemaVersion` moves only on a breaking change: keys are added between versions, so read the ones you know and ignore the rest. The authority is Pinpoint/HandoffDocument.swift; this file is its published restatement.

version.description: Marketing version of the app that wrote the file, e.g. "0.7.0".

generatedAt.description: When this document was written (ISO 8601 with offset).

capturedAt.description: When the screenshot itself was taken, which can be days earlier — a capture is reopened from the history and re-exported. Read from the accessibility snapshot, so absent when that feature was off or unauthorized. Same instant as accessibility.capturedAt when both are present.

task.description: The framing written above the user's instructions in capture.md.

preset.description: The stable token — the only field here meant to be switched on. "raw" means the user asked for no framing.

label.description: The preset's name as the editor showed it, in the user's language.

guidance.description: The paragraph that went into capture.md, verbatim and in the user's language, so a consumer building its own prompt can reuse the same framing. Absent for "raw".

image.description: The image this document describes, and the pixel grid every coordinate below is expressed in. Not necessarily the capture's own dimensions: the clipboard copy is downscaled to stay pasteable.

path.description: Absolute path of the annotated PNG sitting next to this file. Absent when the JSON was exported on its own.

scale.description: Image pixels per screen point — 2 for a Retina capture at native resolution, less once downscaled. With source.screenRect, this is what turns a pixel here back into the point on screen it was read from. Absent when the captured region isn't known.

markerStyle.description: How the numbered badges are drawn on the image.

kind.description: disc: filled badge centred on the point. pointer: map pin whose tip is the point. outline: hollow ring centred on the point.

color.description: sRGB colour every marker and outline is drawn in.

source.description: What was in front of the lens. Every field comes from the accessibility snapshot, so the whole object is absent without one.

application.description: App owning the window under the middle of the capture.

screenRect.description: The region the image covers, in screen points.

markdownPath.description: Absolute path of the Markdown twin next to this file — the same facts in prose. Absent when the JSON was exported on its own.

context.description: The user's instructions, verbatim. Empty string when they wrote none; the key is always present.

accessibility.description: What the accessibility pass contributed overall. Absent when no walk happened (feature off, permission not granted). Present with available: false when a walk happened and came back empty — which is how a consumer tells "not looked at" from "looked at, found nothing".

truncated.description: true when the walk stopped on one of its own limits (time, node budget). A missing element may then mean "not looked at".

secureFieldValuesOmitted.description: Always true. Password fields are never read, at any setting.

textFieldValuesOmitted.description: true unless the user opted into including what is typed in ordinary fields.

markers.description: The numbered badges, ordered by number.

shapes.description: The unnumbered outlines — arrows and rectangles — in the order they were drawn.

point.description: A point in the image, given twice: pixels for an agent working on this file, percentages for one reasoning about a resized copy.

box.description: Axis-aligned rectangle in the image, same dual units as a point. May fall outside the image when it describes an element extending past the captured region.

screenRect.description: A rectangle in screen points, global top-left origin — the space the macOS accessibility APIs speak. Not relative to the image.

id.description: Stable identifier, the same code capture.md prints in brackets. Survives the renumbering that follows a deletion, so two handoffs of one session name the same marker the same way.

label.description: What is drawn on the image: "M1", "M2"… Unlike id, this changes when an earlier marker is deleted.

note.description: The user's description. Empty when they left it blank.

accessibility.description: The interface element under position, resolved against the snapshot taken at capture time. Absent when there is none — the normal case for a capture of something that isn't an app window, or with the feature switched off.

from.description: Arrow: the tail. Rectangle: its top-left corner.

to.description: Arrow: the tip, where the head is drawn. Rectangle: its bottom-right corner.

element.description: An interface element read from the macOS accessibility tree while the capture was being taken. This is what turns a marker from a pixel into something with a name in somebody's source code.

role.description: Raw accessibility role, e.g. "AXButton". Not translated into prose on purpose — it is the vocabulary every inspector shares.

label.description: AXDescription — what a screen reader announces.

identifier.description: AXIdentifier, usually the accessibilityIdentifier written in the app's own source. The most directly actionable field here.

help.description: AXHelp, collected only when nothing else named the element.

value.description: The element's value. Present only when the privacy policy allows it — see redacted.

redacted.description: Why value is absent: secureField (a password field, never read) or textFieldPolicy (withheld by default). Absent when the element simply has no value worth reporting.

box.description: The element's rectangle in this image's pixel grid.

screenFrame.description: The same rectangle in screen points, for a consumer that wants to go back and drive the live UI.

path.description: The containers around the element, outermost first, each rendered as `AXRole "Name"`, ending with the element itself.
